text:
Kailer Yamamoto has played only ten games for Utah this season, with a stint on injured reserve in early November reported by CBS Sports and Pro Hockey Rumors, but our data has him back on the ice in Vegas on Nov. 11 for 18 minutes. When he plays, the Mammoth control the ice.

With Yamamoto on at 5v5, Utah has 59% of shot attempts and 68% of expected goals, 13 points better than without him. Seven points in ten games, and his three goals sit close to his 3.41 expected goals, so this is not a shooting heater. Ten games is a small sample, but it fits what Evolving-Hockey saw last season: two wins above replacement, 53rd among forwards, and elite chance suppression (98th percentile).

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the style: a setup man (84th percentile in primary shot assists) whose offense lives in transition, with 53% of his shots off the rush.

He is a middle-six winger who makes his line better at both ends. Staying healthy is the thing to watch.
headline: Yamamoto's minutes are some of Utah's best
